name: Oklahoma
sources: 2026 rates and brackets (0% / 2.5% / 3.5% / 4.5%; head of household uses the joint table): 2025 HB 2764, enrolled, amending 68 O.S. 2355(D) (legiscan.com/OK/text/HB2764/id/3243767/Oklahoma-2025-HB2764-Enrolled.pdf)

Standard deduction $6,350 / $12,700 / $9,350, $1,000 per exemption, itemizing follows the federal choice, $17,000 itemized cap excluding medical and charity, state income tax not deductible: 2025 Form 511 instructions (oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/individuals/current/511-Pkt.pdf)
provisional: Standard deduction, $1,000 exemptions and the $17,000 itemized-deduction cap are from the 2025 Form 511 instructions (fixed in statute, not indexed)
The $17,000 itemized cap is applied to married filing separately returns unchanged; the instructions do not give a separate amount
notes: Oklahoma caps itemized deductions other than medical and charity at $17,000 in total; this estimate applies the cap to property tax only.
Oklahoma's child tax credit (5% of the federal credit, federal AGI $100,000 or less) is not included.
